## Lib/eacp/Graphics/Menu/MenuCommands.h

- enum class `MenuEntryKind` — eacp::Graphics — MenuCommands.h:29 — What a builder should do with one item, and — the point of it existing — the single place that decides which items consume a command id.
  - `Separator` = 0 — Draws a rule, consumes no id.
  - `Submenu` = 1 — Recurse into it. The header itself consumes no id.
  - `Command` = 2 — Consumes an id and can be chosen.
  - `Skipped` = 3 — Present in the model and absent from this backend — a responder-selector item, which is macOS routing a command down its own chain.
- fn `MenuEntryKind classifyMenuEntry(const MenuItem& item)` — eacp::Graphics — MenuCommands.h:48 — The one definition of the precedence.
- struct `MenuCommand` — eacp::Graphics — MenuCommands.h:51 — One runnable item, flattened out of the tree.
  - field `unsigned int id` — :53
  - field `MenuAction action` — :54
  - field `MenuEnabled isEnabled` — :55
  - field `MenuChecked isChecked` — :58 — Null when the item is not checkable — see MenuChecked.
- fn `Vector<MenuCommand> flattenCommands(const MenuBar& bar, unsigned int firstId)` — eacp::Graphics — MenuCommands.h:71 — Every actionable item in the bar, depth-first, ids assigned from `firstId`.
- fn `const MenuCommand* findCommand(const Vector<MenuCommand>& commands, unsigned int id)` — eacp::Graphics — MenuCommands.h:75 — Null when no command carries that id, which is the case for every WM_COMMAND that came from something other than this menu bar.
- fn `std::string acceleratorText(const KeyEquivalent& shortcut)` — eacp::Graphics — MenuCommands.h:89 — "Ctrl+Shift+P". The text a Win32 menu prints after the tab in its label.
